words.gloss: from the application of the siddha

hindi: सिद्ध-प्रयोग के बाद शंका, वस्तु और कर्म के आधार पर पकड़ा जाता है।
english: After the application of the siddha: seizure by suspicion, by the object and by the act.
notes: Heading of the chapter's method. siddha-prayoga is taken literally ('application of the siddha'; siddha = holy man in the glossary); it may refer to a previously described contrivance, sense not settled. The verb is not supplied by the Sanskrit; the Hindi 'पकड़ा जाता है' is a bare copula-like supply and the English leaves it open. rūpa is rendered 'object' (the thing itself) in the compound rūpa-abhigraha; the alternative 'form/appearance' is possible. ūrdhvam with ablative = after.

words.gloss: with contrary statements of place, caste, lineage, name, work
in meat, liquor, delicacies, food, scents, garlands, clothes, ornaments
moving in secluded spots, forest, gardens, at wrong times
one who has secret treatment done
in contact with despised work, treatises, implements
moving in the shade of covering walls
seller at wrong place and time
in whom hostile intent has arisen
on seeing the nāgarika and high officials

words.gram: pres. part. apa-√sṛ, m. acc. sg.

words.gloss: with dry, altered voice, face, colour
frightened at the approach of armed men
of those living by violence, theft, misappropriation, para-prayoga, secrecy

hindi: जिसकी दायभाग-सम्पत्ति और कुटुम्ब क्षीण हो गए हों, जिसकी आय थोड़ी हो, जिसके देश, जाति, गोत्र, नाम और कर्म के कथन विपरीत हों, जिसकी जीविका और कर्म छिपे हुए हों; जो मांस, सुरा, खाद्य पदार्थ, भोजन, गन्ध, माला, वस्त्र और आभूषणों में आसक्त हो, अत्यधिक व्यय करने वाला हो, कुलटा स्त्रियों, द्यूत और मद्य बेचने वालों में आसक्त हो; जो बार-बार प्रवास में रहता हो, अज्ञात स्थानों में जाता हो, एकान्त स्थानों, वनों, उद्यानों में और असमय घूमता हो, छिपे हुए अथवा मांस वाले स्थान में बहुत मन्त्रणाएँ करता हो; जो ताज़ा घावों का गुप्त उपचार करवाता हो, सदा घर के भीतर रहता हो, पास पहुँचने वाला हो, स्त्री-परायण हो; जो दूसरों की सम्पत्ति, पराई स्त्रियों, द्रव्य और घरों के विषय में बार-बार पूछता हो, निन्दित कर्म, शास्त्र और उपकरणों के संसर्ग में हो; जो रात में ढकी हुई दीवारों की छाया में विचरता हो, विरूप द्रव्यों को अनुचित देश और काल में बेचता हो, जिसमें वैर का आशय उत्पन्न हुआ हो, जो हीन कर्म और जाति का हो; जो अपना रूप छिपाता हो, जो चिह्न से आलिङ्गिन हो अथवा भिन्न आचार वाला लिङ्गी हो, जिसके पूर्वकृत अपदान हों, जो अपने कर्मों से निर्दिष्ट हो; जो नागरिक और महामात्रों को देखकर छिपता हो, खिसक जाता हो, बिना श्वास के बैठता हो, घबराया हुआ हो, जिसका स्वर, मुख और वर्ण सूखा और बिगड़ा हुआ हो; जो हाथ में शस्त्र लिए मनुष्यों के आ पड़ने से डरता हो — ऐसे व्यक्ति पर हिंसा, चोरी, निधि और न्यास के अपहरण, पर-प्रयोग अथवा गुप्त जीविका से जीने वालों में से किसी एक होने की शंका करे। यह शंका से पकड़ना है।
english: [A man] whose inheritance and family are depleted; of small income; whose statements of country, caste, lineage, name and work are contrary; of concealed livelihood and work; addicted to meat, liquor, delicacies, food, scents, garlands, clothes and ornaments; who spends excessively; addicted to unchaste women, gambling and liquor-dealers; who often lives abroad; who goes to unknown places; who moves about in secluded spots, forests, gardens and at wrong times; who holds many consultations in a hidden place or a place with meat; who has secret treatment given to fresh wounds; who is always indoors; who approaches [others]; who is devoted to a woman; who often asks about others' possessions, others' women, goods and houses; who is in contact with despised work, treatises and implements; who moves at night in the shade of covering walls; who sells misshapen articles at the wrong place and time; in whom hostile intent has arisen; of low work and birth; who conceals his form; who is an āliṅgin by a mark, or a mark-bearer (liṅgin) of different conduct; with deeds done earlier (apadāna); pointed out by his own deeds; who hides on seeing the nāgarika and the high officials, slinks away, sits without breath, is agitated, with dry and altered voice, face and colour; who is frightened at the approach of men with weapons in hand: one should suspect [him to be] one or another of those who live by violence, theft, misappropriation of treasure-troves and deposits, para-prayoga, or secrecy. — Such is seizure by suspicion.

text_flags.why: possible: vaira-āśaya (hostile intent) needs a long ā; the printed short a gives vaira-śaya
possible: the root appears as gūh- in vigūhamāna (same unit); guh- is also a valid form, so only a possible variant
possible: śastra (weapon) would suit 'implements', but śāstra (treatise) is also readable; the printed form is translated

notes: One long chain of accusative descriptions of a man, closed by anyatamaṃ śaṅketa; the Sanskrit gives no noun for the man, so '[A man]' and '[him]' are bracketed in English. Doubtful words: nirveśa (rendered 'income'; 'wages, enjoyment' also possible); śauṇḍika (liquor-dealers; tavern-keepers possible); niṣkuṭa (gardens; sense uncertain); sa-āmiṣa (with meat; 'with bait/spoil' possible); abhyadhigantāram (one who approaches, no object stated, low confidence); śāstra (printed; treatise, see text_flags); liṅgena āliṅginam (a '-' unsandhied join; āliṅgin literally 'embracing', so the phrase is rendered literally and its sense is not settled); liṅgin = mark-bearer (not glossed as ascetic); apadāna = deed; anucchvāsa-upaveśin = sitting without breath (not 'breathing freely' etc.); para-prayoga = application of/by others, obscure; the compound hiṃsra-...-ājīvinām is read as 'of those living by violence, theft, ... secrecy'. nāgarika is kept as a title (the town officer), and nāgarika-mahā-mātra is read as a dvandva 'nāgarika and high officials'; 'nāgarika-mahāmātra' as one compound ('high officials of the town') is possible. The closing iti is glossed 'closing particle' and rendered 'Such is' per the glossary.

hindi: वस्तु के आधार पर पकड़ में — खोई और चुराई हुई, न मिलने वाली वस्तु की सूचना उसी प्रकार के व्यापारियों को दे।
english: As for seizure by the object: one should report the lost and stolen [article], which is not to be found, to the dealers of that kind.
notes: The lone '-' is the e-text's join mark after a heading (kept as a token). nivedayet has no stated subject (the owner is not named). tajjāta = 'of that kind' (literally 'born from that'); vyavahārin = dealer, trader. avidyamāna = 'not existing / not found'.

words.gram: n. acc. sg., p.p. ni-√vid caus.

hindi: यदि वे उस सूचित वस्तु को पाकर छिपा लें तो सहायता करने के दोष के भागी होंगे।
english: If, having come upon that [article] which was reported, they should conceal it, they would incur the fault of rendering assistance (sācivya).
notes: The subject 'they' (the dealers of unit 3) is not named. sācivya-kara-doṣa is taken as 'fault of rendering assistance (sācivya, complicity)'. Hindi 'सहायता' renders sācivya.

hindi: न जानते हुए वे इस द्रव्य को सौंप देने से छूट जाएँगे।
english: Not knowing, they would be freed by handing over this article.
notes: ajānantaḥ is read as 'not knowing' (that it was a reported article); the object is not stated. atisarga = handing over, giving up.

words.gloss: of the superintendent of the saṃsthā

hindi: और संस्था-अध्यक्ष को बिना सूचित किए वे पुराने बर्तन-सामान को गिरवी न रखें और न बेचें।
english: And without informing the superintendent of the saṃsthā, they should not make a pledge or a sale of old wares.
notes: saṃsthā is left untranslated (commonly 'market'; the word itself means 'establishment'). bhāṇḍa = ware, vessel, goods; 'old wares' is literal. ādhāna = pledging/depositing as a pledge. The Hindi 'बर्तन-सामान' for bhāṇḍa is wider than 'wares'; the reviewer may prefer 'पुराने माल'. The subject 'they' is the dealers.

words.gram: n. nom. sg., p.p. ni-√vid caus.

words.gloss: the one seized with the object

hindi: यदि वह सूचित वस्तु मिल जाए तो वस्तु के साथ पकड़े गए व्यक्ति से स्रोत पूछे — “तुमने यह कहाँ से पाया?”
english: If that reported [article] should be found, he should ask the one seized with the object about its source: “From where was it obtained by you?”
notes: āsādyeta is taken as a passive optative ('should be found'). The subject of pṛcchet is not stated. The closing iti only closes the quotation and is not rendered. The quotation is opened and closed in the e-text.

hindi: यदि वह कहे — “उत्तराधिकार से प्राप्त हुआ; अमुक से पाया हुआ, खरीदा हुआ, बनवाया हुआ, गिरवी रखा हुआ या छिपाया हुआ; यह इसके प्राप्त होने का स्थान और काल है; यह इसका मूल्य-भाव, परिमाण, चिह्न और मूल्य है” — तो उसके स्रोत के सिद्ध हो जाने पर वह छूट जाए।
english: If he should say: “Obtained from inheritance; obtained from so-and-so; bought; caused to be made; pledged or concealed; this is the place and time of the encountering of it; this is its price, measure, mark and value” — then, when his source is established, he would be freed.
notes: Doubtful: ādhi-pracchannam — read as 'pledged or concealed' (two states); a tat-puruṣa 'concealed by/as a pledge' is possible. upasamprāpti is rendered 'encountering' per the glossary (9.7); 'acquisition' is the natural English sense. argha = price, mūlya = value (both kept distinct). The quotation closes before iti, which is not rendered. dāyādya = what comes from heirs (inheritance).

hindi: यदि खोने वाला उसी को पहचान ले, तो जिसका पहले का और दीर्घ काल का उपभोग हो, अथवा जिसका स्थान शुद्ध हो, उसे जाने — “वह द्रव्य उसी का है”।
english: If the loser should identify that very [article], then of him whose enjoyment [of it] is earlier and long, or whose place is pure, one should know: “The article is his.”

text_flags.why: possible: yasyā is feminine; no feminine noun is present, yasya (m./n. gen.) fits

notes: The syntax of 'yasya pūrvo dīrghaś ca paribhogaḥ śucir vā deśaḥ' is loose; read as 'whose earlier and long enjoyment, or whose pure place'. The sense of 'pure place' (śuci deśa) is uncertain (clean/unblemished place of acquisition?). nāṣṭika = one who has lost (naṣṭa) something. The closing iti closes the quoted judgment 'The article is his'. The Hindi 'उसे जाने' supplies the object of vidyāt, which is only implicit.

words.gloss: produced from material of one origin by one maker

hindi: क्योंकि चौपायों और दोपायों में भी रूप और चिह्न की समानता होती है; तो एक ही योनि के द्रव्य से, एक ही कर्ता द्वारा बने हुए कुप्य, आभूषण और बर्तन-सामान की तो बात ही क्या।
english: For even among quadrupeds and bipeds there is similarity of form and mark; how much more [so] with raw materials, ornaments and wares produced from material of one origin by one maker.
notes: kim aṅga punar is an idiom 'how much more'. eka-yoni-dravya-kartṛ-prasūta is rendered 'produced from material of one origin by one maker'; the original may mean 'produced by a maker from material of one source' (the number 'one' may attach to the maker or only to the source). kupya = raw materials (glossary); the Hindi 'बर्तन-सामान' for bhāṇḍa as in unit 6. The closing iti ends an unquoted reason and is not rendered. Hindi 'की तो बात ही क्या' carries the idiom kim aṅga punar.

hindi: यदि वह कहे — “माँगा हुआ, खरीदा हुआ, गिरवी रखा हुआ, निक्षेप, उपनिधि अथवा अमुक का सेवा-कर्म” — तो उसके अपसार से जोड़ देने पर वह छूट जाए।
english: If he should say: “Borrowed; bought; pledged; a deposit; a sealed deposit; or service work of so-and-so” — then, by connecting [it] with his apasāra, he would be freed.
notes: apasāra is kept untranslated (Kangle takes it as the person to whom he points back as the source; the word literally means 'retreat, withdrawal'; sense not settled; different from the 10.2 'place of retreat'). upanidhi taken as 'sealed deposit' (literally 'placed near'), low confidence on the distinction from nikṣepa. vaiyāvṛtya-karma = work of service, literally; 'of so-and-so' attaches to the whole list. 'it' in 'connecting [it]' is supplied.

words.gloss: the one seized with the object
by givers, those who cause giving, recorders, receivers, observers

hindi: यदि अपसार कहे — “ऐसा नहीं है”, तो वस्तु के साथ पकड़ा गया व्यक्ति दूसरे के देने का कारण, अपने ग्रहण करने का कारण अथवा संकेत को, देने वाले, दिलाने वाले, लिखने वाले, ग्रहण करने वाले, देखने वाले अथवा सुनने वालों के द्वारा मिलाकर सिद्ध करे।
english: Or if the apasāra should say, “Not so,” the one seized with the object should bring together the reason of the other's giving and of his own receiving, or the indication, through givers, those who cause the giving, recorders, receivers, observers or hearers.
notes: pratisamānayet is rendered literally 'bring together'; 'verify, trace back, prove' are the likely senses and are left to the reviewer. nibandhaka = one who records/fixes in writing (low confidence). upaliṅgana = indication, trace. apasāra kept untranslated as in unit 11. The quotation “na-evam” is opened and closed correctly; iti is not rendered. vā after brūyāt joins this rule with the preceding case.

words.gloss: of one who found abandoned, lost, fallen [things]
by the indication of place, time, acquisition

hindi: छोड़ी हुई, खोई हुई, गिरी हुई वस्तु को पाने वाले की शुद्धि देश, काल और प्राप्ति के संकेत से होती है।
english: For one who has found [something] abandoned, lost or fallen, there is clearing (śuddhi) through the indication of place, time and acquisition.
notes: The compound ujjhita-pranaṣṭa-niṣpatita-upalabdha is read as 'found [what was] abandoned, lost, fallen' (a bahuvrīhi/upapada compound); 'lābha' = acquisition (glossary). śuddhi = clearing, acquittal; the verb 'is' is supplied.

hindi: जो शुद्ध न ठहरे वह उसे और उतना ही दण्ड के रूप में दे।
english: One not cleared should pay that and as much [again] as a fine.
notes: tat refers to the article or its value (not stated). tāvat 'so much' is rendered 'as much [again]'; the Hindi says 'उतना' only. daṇḍa here = fine.

hindi: अन्यथा वह चोरी का दण्ड पाए। यह वस्तु के आधार पर पकड़ है।
english: Otherwise he would incur the punishment for theft. — Such is seizure by the object.
notes: daṇḍa here = punishment (not fine). bhaj taken as 'incur, share in'. The closing 'iti rūpa-abhigrahaḥ' is a section label rendered 'Such is', per the glossary.

words.gloss: means of placing and taking hidden goods

hindi: कर्म के आधार पर पकड़ में — लुटे हुए घर में प्रवेश और निकास यदि दरवाज़े से न हुआ हो, दरवाज़े का जोड़ पर अथवा बीज से भेदन, सबसे ऊपरी घर की जाली, वात-अयन और नीप्र का भेदन, चढ़ने और उतरने में दीवार का भेदन, अथवा छिपाए हुए द्रव्य को रखने और लेने के उपाय के रूप में नीचे खोदना, संकेत से जाना जा सकने वाला भीतर का काटना, उत्कर, मसलना और उपकरण — इसे भीतर से किया हुआ जाने।
english: As for seizure by the act: if, of the robbed house, the entry and exit is not by the door; a piercing of the door at the joint or by a seed; a piercing of the lattice, air-hole and nīpra of the uppermost house; a piercing of the wall in climbing up and down; or a digging beneath as the means of placing and taking hidden goods; what is found by indication, the inner cutting, the heap, the rubbing and the implements — one should know it to be done from inside.
notes: GROUPING: none. Hard unit; the whole is a list of accusatives governed by vidyāt, with 'if' supplied only for the first item (the Sanskrit has no 'if'). Doubtful: bīja (seed; 'bolt/pin' is possible); uttama-agāra (uppermost house; 'best/main house' possible); nīpra (obscure, kept untranslated; 'eaves' is a guess); ārohaṇa-avataraṇe (locative, 'in climbing up and down'); upadeśa-upalabhya (found by indication; sense not settled); abhyantara-cheda-utkara-parimarda-upakaraṇa (read as a dvandva of four items: inner cutting, heap, rubbing, implements; utkara = heap, parimarda = rubbing/crushing); the case of gūḍha-...-upāya (neuter or masculine upāya). Hindi 'सबसे ऊपरी घर' for uttama-agāra. The lone '-' after tu is the e-text join mark.

hindi: इसके विपरीत होने पर बाहर से किया हुआ, दोनों ओर से होने पर दोनों के द्वारा किया हुआ जाने।
english: In the reverse [case, one should know it] done from outside; on both sides, done by both.
notes: 'vidyāt' is understood from unit 16 (supplied in brackets in English, bare in Hindi). viparyaya = the opposite of the signs in unit 16. ubhayataḥ is written ubhayata before ubhaya (visarga lost by sandhi).

words.gloss: in a case done from inside
with dry, altered voice, face, colour
with limbs inflamed from climbing high
with body and clothes cut, scraped, split, torn
with hands and feet callused and inflamed
with hair and nails full of dust
with hair and nails cut, broken
with hands and feet just washed
with same garland, liquor, scent, cloth-piece, ointment, sweat

hindi: भीतर से किए हुए कर्म में पास का मनुष्य, व्यसनी, क्रूर सहायकों वाला, चोरों के उपकरणों के संसर्ग में रहने वाला, अथवा दरिद्र कुल की या दूसरे में आसक्त स्त्री; अथवा वैसे ही आचरण वाले परिचारक-जन; अत्यधिक सोने वाला, नींद से थका हुआ, घबराया हुआ, जिसका स्वर, मुख और वर्ण सूखा और बिगड़ा हुआ हो, अस्थिर; अत्यधिक बोलने वाला, ऊँचा चढ़ने से जिसके अंग सूजे हुए हों, जिसका शरीर और वस्त्र कटा, घिसा, फटा और चिरा हुआ हो, जिसके हाथ-पैरों में घट्ठे पड़े और सूजन हो; जिसके केश और नख धूल से भरे हों, अथवा केश और नख कटे या टूटे हों, जो भली-भाँति नहाया और लेप लगाए हो, जिसका शरीर तेल से मला हो, या जिसके हाथ-पैर तुरन्त धोए गए हों; धूल वाले और फिसलन वाले स्थानों में जिसके पैरों के निशान एक जैसे पड़ते हों, अथवा प्रवेश और निकास में जिसके माला, मद्य, गन्ध, वस्त्र के टुकड़े, लेप और पसीना एक जैसे हों — उसकी परीक्षा करे।
english: In a case done from inside, one should examine: a man who is close [to the house], given to vice (vyasana), with cruel companions, in contact with thieves' implements; or a woman of a poor family or attached to another; or attendant people of that kind of conduct; one sleeping too much, wearied by sleep, agitated, with dry and altered voice, face and colour, unsteady; talking too much, with limbs inflamed from climbing high, with body and clothes cut, scraped, split and torn, with hands and feet callused and inflamed; with hair and nails full of dust, or with hair and nails cut or broken; well bathed and anointed, with body rubbed with oil, or with hands and feet just washed; with equal foot-placings in dusty and slippery [places]; or whose garland, liquor, scent, cloth-piece, ointment and sweat are the same at entry and exit.

text_flags.why: stray full stop; the '.' compound mark is out of place, a comma is expected as after the other items

notes: Doubtful: nidrā-klānta (wearied by sleep; 'by lack of sleep' possible); kiṇa (callus); saṃrabdha (inflamed, swollen); pāda-pada (foot-placing, footprint); tulya in the last compound is read as covering all items (same garland, liquor, scent, cloth-piece, ointment, sweat) at entry and exit, so the compound is a bahuvrīhi; vastra-cheda = piece of cloth; vyasanin = given to vice (vyasana). The Sanskrit has 'āsannam' with no object (close to the house is supplied only in brackets in English). The Hindi supplies no object either.

hindi: उसे चोर अथवा परस्त्रीगामी जाने।
english: One should know [him] to be a thief or an adulterer.
notes: pāradārika = one who goes to another's wife. 'him' is supplied (the person examined in unit 18).

hindi: गोप सहित स्थानिक और प्रदेष्टा बाहर चोरों की खोज करे, और नागरिक दुर्ग के भीतर कथित कारणों के आधार पर।
english: The sthānika with the gopa, and the pradeṣṭṛ, should make the search for thieves outside; and the nāgarika inside the fort, on the grounds stated.
notes: Titles kept untranslated: sthānika, gopa, nāgarika (nāgarika = town officer, not 'citizen'); pradeṣṭṛ stays pradeṣṭṛ per the glossary. kuryāt is singular for several subjects (common). The grounds 'nirdiṣṭa-hetu' refer to the signs of units 2 and 16-18. The closing marks (danda) are not part of the tokens. A metrical verse (two lines).
